about: sha256 of each sample city's city_model.json (citygen build output, M10 (stable ids: every id from what the entity is and where it sits, renamed by one pass before the props and at the end; blocks from the road pieces that touch a district, unioned along a Z-order merge tree, so a far change does not move them; the props, plants and gameplay layer draw on stable ids) on M12 on M9 and M11: M12 (stack and turbine interchanges; no sample has two highways crossing with room for one, so every model is the M9 and M11 one byte for byte apart from spec_sha256, which hashes the filled spec and so its new defaults highways.crossings and highways.named[].reuse) on M9 tunnels (nexus_city: a cut-and-cover tunnel under Midtown, peninsula_city: an immersed tube; the metro lowered under foundations, pedestrian underpasses) and M11 (the gameplay layer: points of interest, zones, wealth, danger and police fields, street densities, parking, travel points and sign slots, district params gain wealth, danger and police) on M8c on M8d: M8b on M8a, the trumpet with one loop and one flyover (M8d, only vesper_bay has a trumpet), and transit that passes on a city's first layout: flying loops as Dubins rings, open lines off the roads or as Dubins paths where the roads fail them (M8c); archipelago_free_port is unchanged from M8b). The same bytes on every machine with the pinned requirements: produced for M10 on M12, M9 and M11 (and before it M12 on M9 and M11, M11 on M9, M9, M11 and M8c) on the M4 Mac and, byte for byte, on x86_64 Linux (docker, linux/amd64); earlier milestones confirmed with GEOS 3.14.1 rebuilt with clang against libc++ (the C++ library of macOS builds) and with one worker and another PYTHONHASHSEED; traces of every stage are in docs/progress/M1b_det/ (M1b), docs/progress/M2/<city>/trace.json (M2), docs/progress/M3/<city>/trace.json (M3) and docs/progress/M3p/<city>/trace.json (M3p) docs/progress/M5/<city>/trace.json (M5) docs/progress/M6/<city>/trace.json (M6), docs/progress/M7/<city>/trace.json (M7a) docs/progress/M7b/<city>/trace.json (M7b), docs/progress/M8a/<city>/trace.json (M8a) and docs/progress/M8b/<city>/trace.json (M8b on M8a), docs/progress/M8d/<city>/trace.json (M8d) and docs/progress/M8c/<city>/trace.json (M8c on M8d), docs/progress/M11/<city>/trace.json (M11) and docs/progress/M9/<city>/trace.json (M11 on M9), docs/progress/M12/<city>/trace.json (M12 on M9 and M11), docs/progress/M10/<city>/trace.json (M10 on M12, M9 and M11). blockout_plans change with M9 (tunnel geometry) and not with M11 (the layer adds no blockout geometry) nor with M12 (no sample has a stack); they change with M10 (block corners and the props and plants, which draw on stable ids). tests/test_roads.py asserts them on every run. blockout_plans: sha256 of each sample's blockout_plan.json (citygen blockout, M4), asserted by tests/test_blockout.py; the plan is the same bytes on every machine, Blender only draws it. terrain_cities (M13 on M10): sha256 of the hilly sample's city_model.json (cities/cragmouth), asserted by tests/test_terrain.py with its blockout plan under blockout_plans; the flat samples, the pinned and the stack demo are byte-identical to M10 (M13 changes nothing on a city without terrain; their reports gain the five terrain checks, passing with nothing to check); traces in docs/progress/M13/<city>/trace.json. cragmouth's blockout plan changes with M15 (one object per retaining wall, named by its id, for the Unreal exporter's keys; the model is the same). Greyhook reshape (its coastline made more natural and interesting: a peninsula that fans out into headlands, coast.headlands): peninsula_city's model and blockout plan change, the four other samples, the pinned demo and the stack demo are unchanged; produced on the M4 Mac. deck_cities (M14 on M13): sha256 of the layered sample's city_model.json (cities/vesper_bay_decks, Vesper Bay with a deck over Highcrest), asserted by tests/test_decks.py with its blockout plan under blockout_plans; every city without decks is byte-identical to M13 (the new level and deck fields are left out of the JSON at their defaults; their reports gain no checks, the five deck checks run only when a city has a deck). Stage 1 fixes (after M15): cragmouth's model and blockout plan change (a junction of local roads is level on its grade lines along each leg out to the junction polygon's edge, past its curb and sidewalk corners, so its roads meet at one height there: more retaining walls on the hills, the same deepest cut and fill); vesper_bay_decks' model and blockout plan change (the deck's streets and ramps carry their district in district_ids, so the blockout joins them per district: d03.deck_road.<tile>, d03.deck_sidewalk.<tile>); every other sample is byte-identical; produced on the M4 Mac. M21 (cyberpunk massing): every sample's model and blockout plan change (tower, slab and megabuilding tower forms; true arcs cut at 1 cm chord sag in place of 12 to 32-gons, megasite circles and ovals included; the 150 m neighbor rule; megabuilding open decks only where both towers reach them; a cluster's podium piece under its tower; skybridges keeping stage 2's corridor margins and clear of traced buildings; District.variety in the filled spec); produced on Windows 11 x86_64 (the PC where the earlier goldens reproduced the Mac's byte for byte).

produced_on.machine: arm64 (M4 Mac), confirmed on x86_64 Linux (docker, linux/amd64)
produced_on.confirmed_on: M8b: x86_64 Linux container citygen-x86 (same sha256 for all five and the pinned demo); M8d: produced on x86_64 Linux (cloud container, Python 3.13.17), Mac identity to be confirmed; M11: produced on the M4 Mac and confirmed byte for byte on x86_64 Linux (container citygen-x86, CITYGEN_WORKERS=3), all five and the pinned demo, stage traces identical; M9 with M11: produced on the M4 Mac and, byte for byte, on x86_64 Linux (container citygen-x86, CITYGEN_WORKERS=3); M12 on M9 and M11: produced on the M4 Mac and confirmed byte for byte on x86_64 Linux (container citygen-x86, CITYGEN_WORKERS=3), all five, the pinned demo and the stack demo, stage traces identical; M10 on M12, M9 and M11: produced on the M4 Mac and confirmed byte for byte on x86_64 Linux (container citygen-x86, CITYGEN_WORKERS=3), all five, the pinned demo and the stack demo, stage traces identical; M13 on M10: all five, the pinned demo, the stack demo and cragmouth produced on the M4 Mac and confirmed byte for byte on x86_64 Linux (container citygen-x86, CITYGEN_WORKERS=3)
